title: Scoring System for Contact Tracing Prioritisation
text: following, read toy dataset included package, contains simulated contact tracing data 30 contacts. contact one exposures, led infection. Data stored inside xlsx files distributed package, practice read data csv xlsx files.

what: Preparing the data: creating a ctdata object
title: Scoring System for Contact Tracing Prioritisation
text: ctdata object list containing three data frames: contact_id: unique identifier contact (required) location: location contact (optional) last_visit_date: date last visit contact (optional) infected: logical indicating whether contact infected (optional) onset_date: date symptom onset (optional) contact_id: unique identifier contact (required) date: date exposure, indicated integer since first exposure; practice, actual dates format YYYY-MM-DD (required) exposure_type: type exposure (e.g. “household”, “funeral”) (required) exposure_type: type exposure, matching found exposures infection_proba: probability infection type exposure (derived infection_proba argument) Infection probabilities (argument infection_proba) can estimated previous contact tracing data, literature, expert opinion. , assume household exposures 20% probability infection, funeral exposures 90% probability infection. Smaller datasets can visualised using plot():
code: x <- make_ctdata(   linelist = linelist,   exposures = exposures,   infection_proba = list(household = 0.2, funeral = 0.9) ) x #> <ctdata>: 30 contact(s), 46 exposure(s), 2 exposure type(s) #>  #> $linelist #> # A tibble: 30 × 5 #>    contact_id location   last_visit_date infected onset_date #>    <chr>      <chr>                <dbl> <lgl>         <dbl> #>  1 1          local_town              NA TRUE             22 #>  2 10         new_city                NA TRUE             11 #>  3 11         new_city                NA TRUE             12 #>  4 12         new_city                NA FALSE            NA #>  5 13         hotspot                  5 TRUE             14 #>  6 14         hotspot                 NA TRUE             20 #>  7 15         hotspot                 27 FALSE            NA #>  8 16         hotspot                 NA FALSE            NA #>  9 17         hotspot                 NA TRUE             11 #> 10 18         local_town              28 FALSE            NA #> # ℹ 20 more rows #>  #> $exposures #> # A tibble: 46 × 3 #>    contact_id  date exposure_type #>    <chr>      <dbl> <chr>         #>  1 1             19 funeral       #>  2 10             2 household     #>  3 10             5 household     #>  4 10            13 funeral       #>  5 11            11 household     #>  6 12            18 funeral       #>  7 13             1 funeral       #>  8 13             8 funeral       #>  9 13            28 household     #> 10 14            15 funeral       #> # ℹ 36 more rows #>  #> $risk #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   exposure_type infection_proba #>   <chr>                   <dbl> #> 1 funeral                   0.9 #> 2 household                 0.2 class(x) #> [1] "ctdata" plot(x)

title: Scoring System for Contact Tracing Prioritisation
text: ctscore computes, contact, probability visit today lead detecting new case. First, need specify incubation period distribution, can provided either vector probabilities (giving p(0 day), p(1 day), p(2 days) …) distcrete object returned distcrete::distcrete(). , generate dummy incubation time distribution discretized Gamma:  can now calculate score using ctscore() function, current date day 31 (, real date practice, YYYY-MM-DD format): prioritising individuals, add_ctscore() attaches scores onto linelist ctdata object: can use simple plot visualise scores contact, can useful prioritising visits:  can use as_tibble() flatten ctdata object single data frame, joining risk table onto exposure. argument by_contact indicates whether return one row per contact (TRUE) one row per exposure (FALSE, default): contact (ID 13) highest score multiple exposures, including several funeral exposures, last seen 26 days ago (day 5, current day 31), ample time symptoms appeared since . fact, linelist recorded contact infected developed symptoms day 14. lowest scoring contact single ‘weak’ exposure 2 days ago, unlikely individual infected, , unlikely developed symptoms yet.
code: incub <- distcrete::distcrete(   "gamma",   interval = 1,   shape = 3.5,   scale = 2.5,   w = 0 )  plot(   incub$d(0:30),   type = "h",   lwd = 6,   lend = 1,   xlab = "Days since infection",   ylab = "Probability of symptom onset",   main = "Incubation time distribution",   col = 2 ) score <- ctscore(x, incub, current_date = 31) score #>          1         10         11         12         13         14         15  #> 0.75160666 0.91833598 0.19675645 0.78488929 0.98886504 0.85942526 0.46260342  #>         16         17         18         19          2         20         21  #> 0.01314619 0.89862699 0.17565593 0.20034744 0.19379145 0.19806789 0.91994096  #>         22         23         24         25         26         27         28  #> 0.19762332 0.08951862 0.17677369 0.22575593 0.19547637 0.16702370 0.81157143  #>         29          3         30          4          5          6          7  #> 0.84863053 0.19969489 0.78407698 0.37251628 0.19462428 0.89302170 0.89053700  #>          8          9  #> 0.42430699 0.28448157 ## ctdata with a `score` column in the linelist xs <- add_ctscore(x, score) xs$linelist |>   ggplot(aes(x = score, y = reorder(contact_id, score))) +   geom_col() +   theme_bw() +   labs(     x = "ctscore (probability of detecting symptoms)",     y = "Contact ID",     title = "Contact tracing scoring"   ) as_tibble(xs) |>   slice_max(score, n = 6) #> # A tibble: 6 × 10 #>   contact_id  date exposure_type infection_proba location last_visit_date infected #>   <chr>      <dbl> <chr>                   <dbl> <chr>              <dbl> <lgl>    #> 1 13             1 funeral                   0.9 hotspot                5 TRUE     #> 2 13             8 funeral                   0.9 hotspot                5 TRUE     #> 3 13            28 household                 0.2 hotspot                5 TRUE     #> 4 21             1 funeral                   0.9 new_city              NA TRUE     #> 5 21            17 household                 0.2 new_city              NA TRUE     #> 6 21            30 household                 0.2 new_city              NA TRUE     #> # ℹ 3 more variables: onset_date <dbl>, p_infected <dbl>, score <dbl> as_tibble(xs) |>   slice_min(score, n = 4) #> # A tibble: 5 × 10 #>   contact_id  date exposure_type infection_proba location   last_visit_date infected #>   <chr>      <dbl> <chr>                   <dbl> <chr>                <dbl> <lgl>    #> 1 16            29 household                 0.2 hotspot                 NA FALSE    #> 2 23            27 funeral                   0.9 local_town              30 FALSE    #> 3 27            19 household                 0.2 local_town              NA TRUE     #> 4 18            10 household                 0.2 local_town              28 FALSE    #> 5 18            24 household                 0.2 local_town              28 FALSE    #> # ℹ 3 more variables: onset_date <dbl>, p_infected <dbl>, score <dbl>

title: Scoring System for Contact Tracing Prioritisation
text: can simulate contact tracing data using sim_ctdata() function. function generates synthetic dataset contacts exposures, can useful testing different follow-strategies evaluating performance scoring system. See ?sim_ctdata details arguments. last_visit_date empty yet simulated follow-strategy. can simulate follow-strategy using sim_followup() function.
code: set.seed(123) sim <- sim_ctdata(   n_contacts = 20,   duration = 30,   incub = incub$r(100),   locations = list(cityA = 0.7, cityB = 0.3),   n_exposures = list(cityA = 2, cityB = c(2, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10)),   infection_proba = list(household = 0.2, funeral = 0.4),   type_proba = list(household = 0.7, funeral = 0.3) ) sim #> <ctdata>: 20 contact(s), 55 exposure(s), 2 exposure type(s) #>  #> $linelist #> # A tibble: 20 × 6 #>    contact_id location last_visit_date infected onset_date infection_date #>    <chr>      <chr>              <dbl> <lgl>         <dbl>          <dbl> #>  1 1          cityB                 NA FALSE            NA             NA #>  2 10         cityA                 NA TRUE             11              7 #>  3 11         cityB                 NA FALSE            NA             NA #>  4 12         cityA                 NA FALSE            NA             NA #>  5 13         cityA                 NA FALSE            NA             NA #>  6 14         cityB                 NA TRUE             19             14 #>  7 15         cityB                 NA TRUE             16              9 #>  8 16         cityA                 NA TRUE             12              4 #>  9 17         cityA                 NA FALSE            NA             NA #> 10 18         cityA                 NA FALSE            NA             NA #> 11 19         cityA                 NA FALSE            NA             NA #> 12 2          cityA                 NA TRUE             23             16 #> 13 20         cityA                 NA FALSE            NA             NA #> 14 3          cityB                 NA FALSE            NA             NA #> 15 4          cityB                 NA FALSE            NA             NA #> 16 5          cityA                 NA TRUE             27             12 #> 17 6          cityB                 NA TRUE             34             25 #> 18 7          cityA                 NA FALSE            NA             NA #> 19 8          cityB                 NA TRUE             16             14 #> 20 9          cityA                 NA FALSE            NA             NA #>  #> $exposures #> # A tibble: 55 × 3 #>    contact_id  date exposure_type #>    <chr>      <int> <chr>         #>  1 1             19 household     #>  2 1             28 household     #>  3 1             29 household     #>  4 10             7 household     #>  5 10            30 funeral       #>  6 11             1 funeral       #>  7 11            25 household     #>  8 12            11 household     #>  9 12            30 funeral       #> 10 13            24 household     #> # ℹ 45 more rows #>  #> $risk #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   exposure_type infection_proba #>   <chr>                   <dbl> #> 1 funeral                   0.4 #> 2 household                 0.2 f <- sim |>   sim_followup(     time = 30,     delay = 5,     duration = incub$q(0.99),     coverage = 0.2,     strategy = "random"   ) f |> as_tibble(by_contact = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 20 × 8 #>    contact_id location last_visit_date infected onset_date infection_date #>    <chr>      <chr>              <dbl> <lgl>         <dbl>          <dbl> #>  1 1          cityB                 40 FALSE            NA             NA #>  2 10         cityA                 NA TRUE             11              7 #>  3 11         cityB                 44 FALSE            NA             NA #>  4 12         cityA                 47 FALSE            NA             NA #>  5 13         cityA                 43 FALSE            NA             NA #>  6 14         cityB                 18 TRUE             19             14 #>  7 15         cityB                 14 TRUE             16              9 #>  8 16         cityA                 NA TRUE             12              4 #>  9 17         cityA                 44 FALSE            NA             NA #> 10 18         cityA                 51 FALSE            NA             NA #> 11 19         cityA                 46 FALSE            NA             NA #> 12 2          cityA                 21 TRUE             23             16 #> 13 20         cityA                 48 FALSE            NA             NA #> 14 3          cityB                 29 FALSE            NA             NA #> 15 4          cityB                 47 FALSE            NA             NA #> 16 5          cityA                 26 TRUE             27             12 #> 17 6          cityB                 32 TRUE             34             25 #> 18 7          cityA                 45 FALSE            NA             NA #> 19 8          cityB                 NA TRUE             16             14 #> 20 9          cityA                 26 FALSE            NA             NA #> # code: x <- make_ctdata(   exposures = tibble::tibble(     contact_id = c(1, 1, 2, 3, 4),     date = Sys.Date() - c(6, 4, 5, 1, 5),     exposure_type = c("normal", "funeral", "normal", "normal", "null")   ),   linelist = tibble::tibble(     contact_id = c(1, 2, 3, 4),     last_visit_date = Sys.Date() - c(2, 1, 1, 3)   ),   infection_proba = list(normal = 0.2, funeral = 0.9, null = 0) )  ## incubation time PMF from day 0 to 7 incub <- c(0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 3, 2, 1)  ## a named vector of scores score <- ctscore(x, incub) score #>         1         2         3         4  #> 0.5266667 0.1000000 0.0000000 0.0000000   ## attach the scores to the ctdata linelist res <- add_ctscore(x, score)  ## do the same with probabilities of infection for each contact ## this can be useful for informing post exposure prophylaxis (PEP) p_inf <- p_infected(x) res <- add_p_infected(x, res) res #> <ctdata>: 4 contact(s), 5 exposure(s), 3 exposure type(s) #>  #> $linelist #> # A tibble: 4 × 6 #>   contact_id location last_visit_date infected onset_date p_infected #>   <chr>      <chr>    <date>          <lgl>    <date>     <list>     #> 1 1          NA       2026-09-16      NA       NA         <NULL>     #> 2 2          NA       2026-09-17      NA       NA         <NULL>     #> 3 3          NA       2026-09-17      NA       NA         <NULL>     #> 4 4          NA       2026-09-15      NA       NA         <NULL>     #>  #> $exposures #> # A tibble: 5 × 3 #>   contact_id date       exposure_type #>   <chr>      <date>     <chr>         #> 1 1          2026-09-12 normal        #> 2 1          2026-09-14 funeral       #> 3 2          2026-09-13 normal        #> 4 3          2026-09-17 normal        #> 5 4          2026-09-13 null          #>  #> $risk #> # A tibble: 3 × 2 #>   exposure_type infection_proba #>   <chr>                   <dbl> #> 1 funeral                   0.9 #> 2 normal                    0.2 #> 3 null                      0    ## incubation as a distcrete object incub <- distcrete::distcrete("gamma", interval = 1, shape = 2, scale = 2.5, w = 0) ctscore(x, incub) #>          1          2          3          4  #> 0.36501065 0.04806079 0.02763199 0.00000000

what: Simulate follow-up for contact tracing data — sim_followup
title: Simulate follow-up for contact tracing data — sim_followup
text: function adds simulated follow-ctdata object generated make_ctdata() simulated via sim_ctdata(). function simulates follow-individual ctdata object, based specified follow-time probability followed . function returns modified ctdata object simulated follow-data added.

title: Simulate follow-up for contact tracing data — sim_followup
code: sim_followup(   x,   time = 1,   delay = 1,   duration = 21,   coverage = 0,   strategy = c("random", "geo_random", "ctscore", "geo_ctscore") )

title: Simulate follow-up for contact tracing data — sim_followup
text: x ctdata object time integer indicating number days run simulation ; starts recent date x, follow-history exposures; defaults 1 day delay integer minimum delay follow-start, first exposure concerned contact; defaults 1 - visit can start day first exposure duration integer indicating number days last exposure contact followed ; usually determined according incubation time distribution; defaults 21 days coverage expected proportion contacts visited time step; defaults 0 - follow-strategy character indicating follow-strategy use simulations; currently available values : "random"; see details section information

title: Simulate follow-up for contact tracing data — sim_followup
text: x columns last_visit_date detection_date updated according follow-strategy.

title: Simulate follow-up for contact tracing data — sim_followup
text: Available follow-strategies (strategy argument) include: "random": individuals visited random every day simulation "geo_random": locations prioritized random every day simulation; many contacts possible visited first chosen location, capacity remains, second, third, etc. "ctscore": individuals prioritized highest ctscore every day simulation "geo_ctscore": geographic locations prioritized according highest ctscore every day simulation; many contacts possible visited first chosen location, capacity remains, second, third, etc.
